utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case, please, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-98-34-T, the Prosecutor versus Naletilic and Martinovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Are you ready to start?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, your cross-examination, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. First of all I would ask that we should go into private session for some moments because of some background problems are at issue now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we will go too the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Witness, I would like you to take a look at this order, and clarify one minor thing maybe. I see an order -- an order dated the 23rd of December, 1993.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: If you take -- I will direct you to the second page, and there is some seal, and signature.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Is it your signature?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Okay. So you were already commander of the 2nd Battalion. Can I be suppose that you are mistaken in the date of your appointment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That may have been a mistake because obviously this was at the end of 1993. I always thought I became the commander at the beginning of 1994. I really thought it was the beginnings of 1994 but I do not dispute this date and document.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you very much. You don't dispute the date either, right? I said "the signature," I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was the commander of the 2nd Brigade but I don't think it matters whether I was appointed ten days earlier or ten days later.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Witness, am I fair --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I get up because I wonder whether my learned friend has any other question concerning this document. If not, I'd like to draw the attention of the Trial Chamber to some other facts related to this document, provided the Prosecutor doesn't have any more question on it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, if your question is mainly concerning the documents, would you please make it after -- in the -- at a later stage? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Yes, you may proceed, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Witness, you just claimed before the Trial Chamber that sabotage group had never been a part of any military unit subordinate to Mr. Mladen Naletilic, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: And you did not have in any of your official documents, in the letterhead, the indication that you were a part of the Convicts Battalion, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: I would like the witness to be shown Exhibit 492, and I would like to take with you again Exhibit 479. 429. And 479.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Witness, I would like you to take a look at this document. But be careful not to --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Be careful not to pronounce your name, please. Do you agree that this document was drawn under your signature?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Sorry for interrupting, which one are we looking at 429 or 479?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you're referring to this document, which says "Convicts Battalion, Ivan Stanic, Cico, Bijelo Polje," Mr. Prosecutor, I see this written on this document but this is ridiculous.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the witness is looking at the -- another document, not the one which the Prosecutor was asking him about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Witness, now we are using the document P429 at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: This is the list of soldiers who should receive apartments.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, this document? This document has no -- there is no basis for this document, because I wasn't the chief of the municipality in Mostar to allocate flats.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: I'm not claiming that you were entitled or -- of the housing in the area. I'm asking you about the list of soldiers presented for the apartments being granted to them. Is it your signature?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't see the signature here.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Do you see any names which are familiar to you in this list?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do. I see the names of my soldiers from the 1st Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Are all of them -- take a look at the list, please, again. Were all of them soldiers of your 1st Battalion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Let's pass on to another document, 479, the first one that you were looking at.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Now, the same question about the signature. Is it your signature?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, now, looking at it, I'd say it was my signature, but the rest, this document, to my mind, is a fabrication. There is one typewriter which typed out the heading, and another typewriter typed out the names, and the rest, so that the document, as a document, is not truthful and I think does not represent a valid document, and that my signature is there, I would say that it was my signature. I don't know. Perhaps somebody else could do it the way I do it. I disagree with the heading of this document. It seems that all these men are mine. I did not go through it. That is from the 1st Battalion. It says here, Convicts Battalion, Ivan Stanic, Cico. There has never existed Ivan Stanic battalion. There was the sabotage platoon in the 1st battalion which was called the Ivan Stanic, Cico battalion. Which has 300 or 400, we had 750 men and here there are only 56 of my men listed here so that this document to my mind is ridiculous. And to me, it's not an authentic document because we were never in the Convicts Battalion. Somebody perhaps was toying with this. Perhaps somebody tried to show that the 1st Battalion was a good battalion and therefore a Convicts Battalion, but if you want to establish some relationship with the Convicts Battalion, which was led by Mr. Naletilic, that -- that has nothing to do with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. Now I will look through the lists of soldiers. I mean two lists of soldiers. You see that Emir Brekalo, Andjelko Zlatic and Ivica Kolobara were your soldiers, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They were my men during a certain period of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Is it correct that on one occasion, they were given an assignment to go to Mostar and to gather the remaining persons of Muslim nationality who resided in Mostar at that time, but were domiciled in the area of Bijelo Polje, Vrapcici and Rastani? The task was to gather such persons so that at the later stage you could change them for Croats who were detained by the Muslims? Am I right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. You are not right, because I was in Bijelo Polje on the left bank throughout. We fought on the front line, controlling M-17 axis from Sarajevo to Mostar, where brigades of the BH Army were stopped. Their task was to gain access to the sea, and I do not think I had any time to walk around Mostar. I didn't walk around. And the office for exchange is something that I was in constant contact with, requesting that my captured men be released, be pulled out from hell.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: I would like the witness to be shown Exhibit 509.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I don't even have to read this. This is not a document that I know, nor did I have a part in this. And these names here, the signatures, it has nothing to do with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Witness, sometime ago, you stated before the Trial Chamber that on some occasions, you were not within your sabotage platoon and some other people were in command. Could you -- could we assume that those people were involved in such actions without your knowledge, or at least without your direct command?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They could not, because I've already said where we had been and what we had been doing. We were on the left bank, and I said what forces were attacking us day and night almost. Every single man, especially from my unit, from my battalion, had to be there. We simply had no respite. And other units came too, to help us. Let me describe the conditions of survival on that side. There was a lake there, across which we had to put barrels, and over them planks, in order to cross to the left bank of the Neretva. There are three dams above Bijelo Polje. They would open all three dams so that all these bridges would be swept away.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: I think that I have to cut you off, because you actually explained the situation. No need to dwell more on this issue and waste our time. Witness, you claim today that you finished the primary school at Bijelo Polje, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: And I suppose that you knew people, most of the people of the area of your age?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I met them in war, by and large, but I knew most people --

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: I suggest --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NS [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: I suggest that you should know the people whose full name was Kolobara.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NS [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Bijelo Polje, there are very many Kolobaras. I do not know which one of them do you mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Did you know a person whose nickname was Droba?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Could you tell his name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that his name was Ivan Skobic. If I'm wrong, it could be Ivan Kolobara. I knew him well by his nickname, but I know who that is, if you're asking me about Droba. He was killed during the aggression on Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Did he have relatives, close relatives, brothers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NS [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the aggression, that night, when we were being killed perfidiously, he and his brothers were killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Did you have any other Kolobara in Bijelo Polje who was a member of the Convicts Battalion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that nobody from Bijelo Polje was a member of the Convicts Battalion, but I do not know which Kolobara you have in mind. You have to give me his full name.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Do you know Miroslav Kolobara?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do, two, and I believe there is a third one too, who is still a boy and who did not participate in the war. Miro or Miroslav. I'd say that is the same name, Miro or Miroslav Kolobara. I mean, Miro could be short, it could be Miroslav.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: I would like the witness to be shown Exhibit 680.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Witness, I would like you first to take a look, to take a look at that part of this document. It's page 2 in B/C/S version, which commences with, "Dana, 19th of November, 1993." This part of the document deals with a certain Ivica Kolobara?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Miroslav Kolobara?

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: No, Ivica Kolobara, if we are on the same page. In the English version, it's also page 2 -- sorry, it's maybe together with all the stuff, maybe page 3. Have you found Ivica Kolobara?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a moment. Oh, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where it says the 13th of November, 1993? Is that it, on the 13th of November, 1993? You mean that passage?

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: The 19th of November.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where it says, "The criminal charges have been brought against Ivica Kolobara? Is that the one.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Yes and that he's a member of the 2nd Brigade of the sabotage platoon. Is that the same Kolobara that you met before in two lists of soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possibly, but I am not sure if he was a member of the 2nd Battalion of the 2nd Brigade, although Vrapcici was in the 2nd Battalion where he comes from. Before that, he was with me. I can't remember if he transferred to the 2nd Battalion of the 2nd Brigade because men from Vrapcici who were with the 1st Battalion at first, after the war with the Serbs, came under the 2nd Battalion of the 2nd Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Now, Witness, let's turn to -- actually, it's on the same page, in the B/C/S version, page 2, just the paragraph, second from the upper side of the page, which starts with Miroslav Kolobara, and in English version, this is page 2.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Am I fair to say that these two people, persons, Ivica Kolobara, and Miroslav Kolobara are close relatives, even brothers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Why do you think so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because I know they were not brothers.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: They have the same father's name, mother's name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Here it says mother, Milika, that is Miroslav Kolobara's mother. And Ivica Kolobara's mother is Mira Peric, and the former one was Milka Kukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Could they be second cousins?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said there were very many Kolobara's in Bijelo Polje but again I do not think so. One used to live in Vrapcici and the other one, as far as I could see in Kuti Livce.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Okay. Let's pass on to another topic. Is it correct, Witness, that your unit participated in military operation on the 24th of August, 1993, in Rastani?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Rastani fell several times into the hands of the BH Army and would be recovered and placed again under our control. If that was the last operation, and I believe you're referring to it, then yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Witness, I refer to a certain operation which took place on the 24th of August, 1993, and I'm asking about this operation.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could not keep up with dates, because I was involved every day in major fighting. I'm saying if that was an action to liberate Rastani, and I think it was September, if that is the date, then I did participate in that operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Witness, I will ask you very direct question, a very direct question. Is it correct that your unit was involved in military operation, together with the soldiers --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Together with?

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: The soldiers subordinate to Mladen Naletilic, Tuta, and that operation took place on the 24th of August, 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think you're wrong. There -- perhaps there is such an action but the action that I took part in involved the 2nd Brigade and the commander of Rastani was Mr. Stampar. We were the ones who liberated Rastani and the Convicts Battalion did not take part in it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honours. We will pass on to Stampar a little bit later.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: But now let's return to Rastani and the 24th of August.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: I would like the witness to be shown Exhibit 573.1. I would like the witness to just leaf down the document and pay special attention to the second page of the document, which is called, "Other occurrences." In English, this is the third page.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Are you seeing the words, the sentence which begins with "the Convicts Battalion took control over Mostar," and so on? And Zeljko Bosnjak and Drazenko Sopta were killed in the fighting? That's maybe the end of this short information.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. You are told me to read the whole passage, and I've just read only one half of it, so will you please wait a little?

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Sorry, sorry.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. You can ask me what you want to know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Do you know of any military operation in Rastani carried out by Convicts Battalion when they took control of the village of Rastani?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. You are talking about a date -- about the date where my command in Bijelo Polje were attacked on the North Camp. At that moment, I had no idea where was who, let alone the Convicts Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Okay. Let's pass on to another document.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: I would like the witness to be shown Exhibit 573.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry, if the Prosecutor can help me, I only have 573.1. I do not have the document 573. Is it in this binder or perhaps I didn't get it. Oh, sorry, sorry, I've found it. I've found it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: My next question will be, Witness, do you see this document 573? I mean the first page? This is an order in the name of Colonel Miro Andric and according to this order, second paragraph, first paragraph, the line is secured, Orlac-Rastani-Mostar, and Tuta's professional unit must be released. Again, it is dated the 24th of August, 1993. The document was sent to HVO 2nd Brigade.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Not to me. I know nothing about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: You don't know, okay.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I repeat that I didn't know where my head was, because all my village had been killed an burnt down and I remained defending myself on the Neretva bank. I cannot tell you anything about this. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Okay. Let's pass on to another document, P574. It's not a long document. You may read it all from the very beginning to the end, paying special attention to sector 4. In English, this is page 3. Have you read it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Do you see, Witness, that a group of 24 soldiers were involved in the operation of liberating Rastani with Tuta's unit? Wasn't it your group of soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm telling you again that my group of soldiers was attacked that night. We defended ourselves, 250 of our men were captured it. What was happening in Mostar, how they were fighting, the North Camp fell, I really cannot tell you anything about it, but as far as I know, as far as I know, and let me tell you, Tuta's unit, in the war against the Muslims, did not exist. There was a unit --

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Witness --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NS [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the war against the Serb or Chetnik aggression, as far as I know. There was Tuta's Convicts Battalion. And this here, these allegations here, I don't know who writes what.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... my questions.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... to answer my questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: I would like the witness to be shown Exhibit 575 and 576. Your Honour, this will be the last -- not the last, the last but one question in this series of questions devoted to Rastani. So let me ask them, please, now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Tell me, what are you interested in?

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Witness, there are two orders with identical content, issued for Miljenko Lasic, commander of the operational zone; and the Chief of Staff, Zarko Tole; to the same effect that the Convicts Battalion and Maka's men, with troops from the 5th Battalion of the HVO 2nd Brigade should be released and replaced by Ludvig Pavlovic unit. What can you explain concerning these two orders? And mentioning Maka's -- Makovi Ljudi?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who Maka's men are. I have heard this term, Mak's or Maka's men for the first time from you and I see it written for the first time in my life. Nobody ever referred to me or to a unit with this name.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Witness, you claimed that it was Milan Stampar who was in charge of Rastani area, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Witness, was it your testimony today that it is Milan Stampar who was in charge of Rastani area in 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Do you know when he was appointed to that position and whom he replaced?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NS [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was appointed to this position following the aggression, and the capturing of Bijelo Polje by BH Army. I'm not sure whether he was -- replaced Mr. Ilija Vrljic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: I would like the witness to be shown Exhibit 577.1.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: This is an order signed by Slobodan Praljak on the 25th of August, 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Witness, do you agree with me that Milan Stampar was appointed commander of Rastani area on the 25th of August, after the village of Rastani had been secured on the 24th of August?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know. I really couldn't tell you which was the date exactly that Milan Stampar was appointed commander. I do know, however, that this happened after this aggression, as I mentioned before, that he was the commander of Rastani and the 2nd HVO Brigade, but I really couldn't given you the exact date because I do not know it and I can't invent it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Your Honour, it seems to me that it is time for the break, and I really I will need not too much time after the break, maximum 15, 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, as you know, we started late.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: If you need 20 minutes, what if we go on for the next 20 minutes? Then we will stop at 4.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Okay. I will try.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Witness, is it correct that somewhere in the autumn, 1993, on one occasion, you visited Siroki Brijeg and interrogated one Muslim prisoner?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is true that I visited Siroki Brijeg and I talked to a member of the army, but I didn't interrogate him.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Isn't it correct that the main issue you discussed with him was one accident when the mine in the area of Rastani -- sorry, the dam was under threat of being mined by some people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NS [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were not talking about this incident, but I can tell you a few words about this event, should you be interested in it. We did talk about people that had been caught -- killed in this accident. I mentioned these individuals and I asked him whether he knew where they could be found, about their whereabouts, but it was not an interrogation. It was a conversation.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Is it, Witness, also correct that that conversation took place in the premises of the tobacco institute in Siroki Brijeg?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Talking to Berko Pusic, who asked -- who requested me to go to the Siroki Brijeg military police station, I went to the military police station and I had this conversation with the individual there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: And on the same day, you did not visit the tobacco station, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: You claim that you knew that person before, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. He used to be my soldier in the war against the Serbs. I think he was one of my men. One used to be one of my men but the other one I didn't know very well. Perhaps he also used to be one of my men.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: My next set of questions. So your headquarters were in Vojno right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Vojno? No, it was on the left bank of the Neretva where the military operations went on. This is where the headquarters were.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Witness, is it correct that there was a sort of detention facility in Vojno which was not registered by the Red Cross?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: You did not have any prisoners in Vojno, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you before that I stayed on the left bank and to my knowledge, there were no prisoners on the right bank in Vojno because this is a very small hamlet along the bank of the River Neretva.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: And you never took prisoners for the 1st Battalion of the 2nd Brigade of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NS [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the left bank, where I was stationed, we had no prisoners whatsoever, and as far as I'm familiar, there were no prisoners in Vojno either, and that Vojno is on the right bank.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: I would like the witness to be shown Exhibit 567.1. The page -- it's not in this binder. There must be an additional binder. Honourable Judges may turn to page with the last four digits 5140. 5140. If it is an issue, maybe this page could be placed on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Do you have it at your hands? I mean the extra copy. Maybe you could use your document, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Yes, on the ELMO. There is no danger that somebody's name will be disclosed now, revealed. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I don't know what you want from me. I can see Vojno written at the top.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Yes, but I don't say anything --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see a few names. I don't know what you want to ask me.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Yes, my question was: And there was a reply that no prisoners were taken to Vojno, and this is the list of prisoners who were taken in the number of 33 persons from Heliodrom to Vojno on the 2nd of September, 1993. What -- could you explain?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I can see the document. As I mentioned before, as far as I know, there were no prisoners in Vojno. They couldn't, under those circumstances, be kept there, and I don't know whether they were there or not. I never saw prisoners there and I really can't tell you anything about that. I was on the left bank. Since we were defending the front line, it wasn't just the 1st Battalion but there were also other units that were helping us. In Vojno, there was the ambulatory, there was the mess and there were soldiers who would serve a shift there. I was on the left bank, and if I was not on the left bank, nobody was allowed to cross to the left bank. I can assure you that that was the situation. And when I would cross to the right bank, I would do it over night, and I had to come back very clearly so that nobody could notice that I had left the left bank. Perhaps there were prisoners but not to my knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: We don't see the transcript, I'm sorry, oh, yes. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: And now I would like the witness to be shown Exhibit 774. Item 60. 774. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: So this is item 60.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Sorry, it doesn't appear to be in our binders.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's a very old exhibit which was admitted a long time ago, so it must be somewhere in our archive binders.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: I see, but not with us, it's not in these binders.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: I have bad luck with binders.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You may proceed, Mr. Poriouvaev.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Thank you. Again we must put the document, the original, on the ELMO. Or the English version. Makes no difference. This is only one page. I think that the witness has the document.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The Judges didn't have it. That's why they asked. But the witness does have the Registrar's copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Please take a look at the list of people under item 60.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Do you see that seven people were killed on the 14th of September, taken to the 1st Battalion, 2nd Brigade by Dragan Sunjic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not possible. I would probably have known about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Okay. In your opinion, it's not possible. But do you --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sure that I would have been familiar with that. Therefore, I don't believe that this is possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Do you have Dragan Sunjic within your unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dragan Sunjic was a member of my unit. Well, in fact, there were more persons by the name of Dragan Sunjic. I think that they were all members of my unit. At a later stage, I think that Dragan Sunjic joined the military police in the period mentioned here, maybe he had already been a member of the military police or maybe he was a member of my battalion, but I don't recall ever having seen him on the left bank.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Do you remember a man whose name was Mario Mihalj?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mario Mihalj, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Mihalj?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Mihalj no. There is no such name, no such person in Bijelo Polje.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Maybe my pronunciation is a little bit wrong. Mihalj?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mihalj, but perhaps, yes, perhaps you're referring to it a person by the name of Mihalj. There are persons by the name of Mihalj there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: I mean Mario Mihalj.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NS [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a Mario Mihalj, who at the beginning of the war, when the Serbs attacked us, was 17 years old and I wouldn't give him a rifle and let him to participate in the fighting. Later on, however, I think that he joined the battalion. I also think that later, he was a member of a military police and then joined the 2nd Professional Brigade, and he was killed on the front line. If this is the Mario Mihalj that you're referring to, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Was he ever a member of your sabotage group?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: And Dragan Sunjic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps he did participate in some combat activities as a volunteer.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: I would like the witness to be shown Exhibit 704. These are digits -- it's an old exhibit, page 27 in the English Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. version, and digits 5383, 5384 in the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We don't have this document in this binder, although -- although on the list, we saw this document, but we could not find it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Your Honour, we use it every now and then, I think. I suppose that it must be somewhere in the Trial Chamber. But we can put it on the ELMO. Yes, first, I think the version in B/C/S, and then maybe in English.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What would you like to know?

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Do you see any names that sound familiar to you in this list?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I know all these names. I haven't gone through the entire list but I think I know them all.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Do you see under number 46, 47, 48?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Dragan Sunjic under 46, Mario Mihalj under 47 and Gordan Skobic under 48?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Can you confirm that they were your soldiers, according to this document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not according to this document, because I don't know what the document's origin is, but these individuals were my soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Okay. The individuals or your soldiers were indicated in that document? That is for the transcript, right?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, Your Honour, I have to draw your attention to a fact now, and later, of course in my redirect, I'll do it again. Your Honours, check the B/C/S original of this document, and the translation. I have both versions in front of me. In the Croatian version, original or copy or whatever it is, has 5383 as the last. Then we have 5382, and then the list of the next unit. And then we have 5384. We don't even know what unit this list refers to, because the list on the page 5382 is a complete list and the list on 5384 is a new list, where nobody can recognise what unit these individuals belong to. And then you have a new unit starting with 5385 and then 5386. In other words, -- well, the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I complete, sir? This is your document. On the next page, 5382, we have the next unit, which is logical. And in the Croatian original, the last name on that page is under item 33. I really do not know where you got this document with 6820, 6820 where you have 45 and 46, 47 and 48, which is on the ELMO. I don't have it here. I also don't have a page 6820, 6820 is something quite different in my version. Now, these are the originals. It's very easy to compare them. I don't see the problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, I think we are in a worse position than you because we don't have that document at our hands. We could not judge whatever you said, but the witness has already answered that question. He said "not according to this document, because I don't know what the document's origin is but these individuals were my soldiers." So this issue is closed. You have the full right to raise any objections concerning the authenticity and origin of this document but not now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] By all means, Your Honours. I have come across a large number of documents similar to this, and to put it very mildly, this is very unusual indeed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, I think there will be plenty of opportunity for to you do that. For instance, in your re-examination, with the Trial Chamber with admitting all those documents. Mr. Prosecutor, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As far as I can recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: And how do you explain that these two orders are signed by you and are dealing with prisoners?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what to tell you about this document, because I do not remember this. I do not remember any prisoners at the Heliodrom, and especially Ljubuski. I've never heard of it, let alone signed something.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Do you see your signature on both orders?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do, yes, yes. From the Heliodrom, these detainees were exchanged while I was still waging war with the BH Army in Bijelo Polje. They were released and then all these detainees then attacked us. Now, could be, of all that war, I do not remember. I really do not remember that I dealt with -- that I handled some prisoners.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have overstepped your limits. That's why I have concluded my cross-examination at this point. Thank you very much for your patience.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. We will have a break. We will resume at 20 minutes to 5.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I shall be very brief.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Only a few questions, Witness. Please be so kind as to tell this Honourable Court, to explain it, to explain how the 2nd Brigade of the HVO in Mostar was organised and how many brigades were there in Mostar? I mean in 1993.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The organisation of the HVO 2nd Brigade, the brigade was made of four battalions, the 1st Battalion, the 2nd Battalion, the 3rd Battalion and the 5th Battalion. In Mostar, there was yet another brigade, and that is the 3rd Brigade, whose composition I do not know.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Who is the commander of the 2nd Brigade and who is his commander?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Until the 30th of June, that is until the attack of the BH Army, of the Muslim aggressor, the commander was Mr. Ilija Vrljic. After that, the commander was Milan Stampar. And the 2nd Brigade was commanded by the operative staff Mostar, with Brigadier Miljenko Lasic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I will not waste time showing you documents. Tell me just one thing. This last document, 704, which was shown you by the Prosecutor, he did not tell you, that is they allege that these are salaries for members of the Convicts Battalion. My question is: Did you ever receive your salary, the 12st Battalion or the 2nd Brigade through the Convicts Battalion? And would that be possible at all?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That would not be possible. No, I do not think that it is possible. Why would it go through the Convicts Battalion if we were receiving our salaries through the 2nd Brigade? That is through the HVO. Through the Ministry of Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I see. Very well. The only document, sir, and I will ask for it, I believe it is here. Will you please just have a look at document 573 and 573.-- 573. Yes, there were two but now I see only one, in the Croatian original, no, no, no, both are here, and 573. Will you please be so kind, where it says, "North sector commander," do you see any signature or a stamp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I do not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And on the other document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Thank you. And now, can I ask our honourable and esteemed Madam Registrar, 731.01? Will you please be so kind, on the first page of this document, but have a good look, do you see anything below, "I order"? Do you see anything underneath? Just look -- have a good look. Do you see that it says, [redacted]?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Will the Honourable Court please look at the Croatian original? You will see, Your Honours, underneath, "I order” [redacted] [redacted] and one can see the outline of the stamp in the Croatian original.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, I believe that we are in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. PORIOUVAEV
utterances.text: Your Honour, excuse me, I would like to clarify the number of the document. Maybe there is some mistake in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Yes, no, no, no. Yes, 731.01, 01.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Are you referring, Mr. Krsnik, to what appears to be a shadow of another document on top of the photocopy? Is that what you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry, I didn't get the interpretation. Not only that, Your Honour, not only that. That is not the only thing I'm trying to say. I want to say that it is quite obviously possible to copy on one and the same sheet of paper anything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: I think that the witness should first be asked, and I think he has been asked, if he recognises his signature. You are now trying to put a proposition to him or a supposition. Do you think that's allowed?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. I asked the witness in advance, "Could he see if there was anything written underneath, "I order" and the witness answered so I can ask him once again.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Witness, would you please be so kind and tell us what you see written underneath, "I order."

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I'm sorry, can we have a redaction, here, please? Your Honour, please, believe me I'm really much too tired. I've made a very serious mistake now. Witness, do not -- please could we go into private session, please and have this redacted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU

utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: At this stage, are there any documents to tender? I guess not on the side of the Defence counsel.

utterances.text: Your Honour, with your leave, I will prepare a submission on the exhibits I intend to tender, just in a couple of days. All right?

utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.text: You may sit down, please. Could I test the microphone? Because I could not hear my own voice through the earphone.

utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll do the testing, testing.

utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.text: You can turn on the second microphone and you don't have to it approach the microphone closer because this could be bothersome for you. You will now get a piece of paper witness, with your name. Please do not pronounce it aloud, if this is your name, please just say yes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: So you are Witness NT, and this -- these are the initials that everybody will be addressing you under in this courtroom. We are trying to protect your dignity and whenever we need to do this, we will ask for a private session so -- but please be careful, do not pronounce your name aloud.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To start with, Your Honours, I apologise, but to be on the safe side, I would ask you to go to private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NT
utterances.text: So a day or two later -- attacked us they were strengthened by the people of Hrasnica who were led by General Fikret Pravljak. And we had four soldiers killed. Our soldiers, our friends. One of them was Juka's deputy Samir Kahvedzic, aka Krusko.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: What happened afterwards?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NT
utterances.text: Afterwards, we withdrew towards Herzegovina. We went through the mountains and we walked for two days, to get to Klis, a village near Konjic. The women, the children, were mistreated on Mount Igman. My girlfriend, who was then pregnant, suffered a great deal as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Your wife is of what ethnic origin?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NT
utterances.text: She is a Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Very well. Now you have arrived in Konjic. I know that it's difficult to recall all the dates and months but when approximately, which month and year, you arrived in Konjic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NT
utterances.text: We left Igman towards the end of January, 1993. And we arrived at Klis. We were there received by the people. We stayed there for a few days. Mr. Prazina, Juka, the general; he left for Mostar. I was waiting in Klis because gradually people were escaping from the Silos Camp, the BH Army detained our members, put them in detention, and some of them were able to escape and arrived in Klis because I was also in Klis. Some four or five days later, Juka came back to Klis and he told us that we should leave for Mostar, where he was able to find accommodation for us in the barracks on the Heliodrom.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Did you get to Mostar? Were you accommodated at the Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: How were you organised? Did you join the HVO? Or what was the situation? Were you treated as refugees or what?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NT
utterances.text: No. We were not refugees. We were accommodated in the barracks on the Heliodrom. There were about 120 of us there. Of these, there were some women, children, some 35 to 40 of them were men. We arrived there in the afternoon hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: My question was whether you joined the HVO units at that time or did you continue to be members of BH Army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NT
utterances.text: Having arrived in the afternoon hours, next morning, Juka stood in front of us and told us that we were members of the Croatian Defence Council and that we were under the Main Staff of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I have a document here. I'll ask the Registrar -- this is Prosecution Exhibit P249. Could you please help me with it? [In English] P249, sorry, excuse me, Madam Registrar. [Interpretation] I apologise, Madam Registrar, for this situation. Thank you very much. [In English] You can put the English version in the ELMO, please. I have the English. You have also the English version? Yeah, okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Are you familiar with this document, Witness?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, can you put so that the Judges can see? [Interpretation] Can you push it further upward, please so that we can see the text?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Witness, could you show the signature, please, on the ELMO? Could you push this document a bit further, to the top? [In English] Like this, okay, okay, okay. [Interpretation] Witness, we are not going to read through this document because it's self-explanatory. Can you only tell us: Is this signature and this stamp on the basis of your knowledge so far --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm continue with my questions. I've noticed that you have now set up a company. Could you tell us who was the commander of your company and who was your direct superior?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we go into private session, please, just in case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we will go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the 9th and 10th of May, 1993, I was at the Heliodrom in Mostar. In the barracks at the Heliodrom.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And do you know anything, do you know if anything -- about anything that came to pass? Was all your unit at the Heliodrom or only you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NT
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Would you tell us what you know about these two dates and your unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NT
utterances.text: I remember two moments on that date, Your Honours. May I explain? In April, in late April, I manned the line beneath Velez, near Mostar, and when we withdrew from the front line, I was in the town of Mostar. I was wounded there with another seven of my soldiers. Of those seven, one was killed on the spot. We were wounded by the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, because they said later that Juka was in the vehicle and they opened fire. On the 9th of May, before that, I was in the hospital, and I was sent home for house care. On the 9th of May, in the morning hours, around 9.00, Juka told me that the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina had attacked and that he had to go to Mostar to be on the reserve for the Ludvig Pavlovic unit. He was there for about two or three hours in Mostar, I mean. He returned. Before that, I stayed back with a squad to guard the Heliodrom barracks because there were very many children and women, and we had gone through that terrible experience on Igman and I stayed there to protect them because there was this attack on Heliodrom.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: You're all telling us about the 9th?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NT
utterances.text: Yes, about the 9th.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And what about the 10th? Did anything special happen on the 10th?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NT
utterances.text: On the 10th, sometime between 12.00 and 1.00, commander Juka called me by radio and told me -- and said to me that there were very many of our people wounded and that I should go to the hospital to look after them, to see what had happened to them. I went to the hospital. We had two men severely wounded. Of them, one was Samir, a Muslim. Another one was Davor, a Serb. One was hit in the head. And the other one in the chest. We had four lightly wounded soldiers, and about 3.00 or 4.00, when I returned to the Heliodrom, Juka asked me, "What about them?" And I told him what I had seen. And he was angry, started shouting at me, and said that he had liberated Vranica and that my friend Alica --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we go into private session, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we will go to the private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In mid-or end of June, Juka Prazina left. He said he was going to the seaside. We waited for him at the Heliodrome. Many people left. Some went to Croatia, to their families. Some went abroad. And about ten days later, I was called to the operative zone in Mostar because I belonged -- where I belonged, and I was told that I had to leave the facility of the Heliodrom barracks because we were too few. After that, we left. We went to a flat in Mostar, and we were there together. We were 12. [redacted] [redacted].

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Don't give us the names, we are in open session. I asked you whenever you give a name that could identify you. Now we have to go into private session. I know it's my fault because I am a professional and you are not. Could we have this name redacted, please, and now go on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NT
utterances.text: And I lived with my wife in that flat, and every day, I was with other men. We were about 12. In another flat, where we were stationed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Now, the 12 of you, did you have any tasks? Did you perform any tasks? How long were you in that flat, that is you, your group, your ten-strong unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NT
utterances.text: Yes. We were still under the Main Staff, operative zone Mostar, and we were still the ATG Krusko, sabotage company.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Weren't you too few for a company? That is if I got your meaning right.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NT
utterances.text: Yes. We were too few for a company but the 12 of us who were there, Juka's, that is where I became a commander later on, we were later on joined by a few more people from Mostar. They came to the unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Very well. And how long did you have that platoon or company or whatever?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NT
utterances.text: In today's system, it was a squad, but we called ourselves a company, and we were in front of the operative zone in Mostar, in front of the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: How long, I asked you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NT
utterances.text: Until the end of 1993, when we moved over to the 2nd Guards Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: My last three questions: Do you know Mr. Mladen Naletilic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NT
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: When did you meet him and for how long did you know him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NT
utterances.text: I met him in March, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I see. My next question is: Was he ever your commander, that is the commander of your unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NT
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And did you ever tell anyone that he was your commander?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NT
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we will break here. We will resume at ten minutes past 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Bos, cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Your Honours, I distributed some exhibits which I intend to use for this witness. The Defence has already received copies and I think you will receive them any minute now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm very happy this binder is in there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: So am I, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness NT, my name is Roland Bos from the Prosecution and I will ask you some questions. Witness, have you ever heard of the name Convicts Battalion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: What do you know about the Convicts Battalion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NT
utterances.text: Well, I heard something but I can't say anything. I don't know anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Well, what did you hear? When did you hear about -- you said that you heard about it. You must have known a bit more than just say that you've heard about it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NT
utterances.text: When I arrived in Mostar, I heard about the Convicts Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Do you know where the Convicts Battalion was stationed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NT
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Do you know who the commander of the Convicts Battalion was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NT
utterances.text: I didn't know it in the beginning. I said I didn't know, because we were new in Mostar. We didn't know anyone. Later on, I heard that Mario Hrkac, Cikota, was the commander of the Convicts Battalion.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Will the witness please not come as close to the microphone?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Don't get so close to the microphone, if you keep a distance of about half a metre, that's fine. Witness, isn't it true that you've said that your unit was called the ATG Krusko, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Isn't it true that this unit was also referred to as the KB Krusko or the Convicts Battalion Krusko?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NT
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: You never heard of that abbreviation for your unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NT
utterances.text: Never heard. When Juka was there, when I stayed behind and took over, it was never the Convicts Battalion Krusko.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: As you testified, that you met Tuta in March, 1993; is that correct? Was that the first time that you met Mr. Mladen Naletilic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NT
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Would you tell the Court where this was and what was -- what was the occasion? Could you give a bit more detail about this meeting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NT
utterances.text: Yes. In Mostar, it was in Mostar in a restaurant, at Edo Bajram's. [redacted].

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Please refrain from mentioning a name unless I specifically ask you because you're a protected witness.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NT
utterances.text: My girlfriend was friends with Mr. Naletilic's friend -- girl -- lady friend. In a restaurant, we met and came to know one another. He asked me, "Who is this?" And I said it was my girlfriend and that she was expecting. He asked me, "Why don't you get married?" And I said that I will marry straight away because it will be -- it would be a honour for me if Mr. Naletilic agreed to be my best man.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Why are you saying this? This is the first time you said you met Mr. Tuta and you're straight away saying it would be a honour if he would be your best man. Could you explain that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NT
utterances.text: Yes, I can. In Mostar, when I personally went out into town, I heard a great deal about him, that he was a legend against Serbs, at the time when the Serbs had their aggression against Bosnia-Herzegovina, and it was a honour for me, and is still a honour for me, to have him as my kum, as my best man.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: So Mr. Naletilic was in fact your best man when you got married to your girlfriend? Is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NT
utterances.text: Yes, and his lady friend was also my kuma.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: When did you get married? May I ask that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NT
utterances.text: In 1993, April.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: And did you get married in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Now, let's go back to the beginning of the establishment of the ATG Krusko. You said -- you've testified about Mr. Juka. What is the relationship between Mr. Juka and Mr. Tuta? Do you know whether they knew each other and how well they knew each other?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NT
utterances.text: I do not know that, because I spent most of my time with Juka, and I am not aware that they were close.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Did you ever see Mr. Juka and Tuta together?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NT
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Witness, is it not true that when you arrived at the Heliodrom it was actually because of Tuta that you were being accommodated at the Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NT
utterances.text: No. That is not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Witness, is it not true that you may have been officially assigned under the command of the operational zone but in fact it was your unit acted under the direct command of Mr. Tuta?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NT
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, before this Honourable Court, and my oath, I speak the truth. We were never the Convicts Battalion or under the command of Mr. Naletilic. We belonged to the -- to the Mostar operative zone, that is the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Very well. Witness, do you recall in October, 1993, so this is after Juka had left the ATG Krusko, do you remember that you were -- you and some other soldiers from Krusko were assigned to an operation under -- under the command of Mr. Stampar, who was the commander of the 2nd Brigade, and who had his area of responsibility in Rastani? This is October, 1993.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NT
utterances.text: When Juka left in October, you are mentioning October, we were a sabotage -- you can call it a squad, a platoon, a company, that is what we were called, for the operative zone in Mostar. That is Mr. Vrljic, who commanded the brigade before him, and then Mr. Stampar, they could alert us and issue me orders at any time.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Could the witness be shown Exhibit P623.1?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Please read the document for yourself and then I will ask you some questions about it. Have you read the document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NT
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Now, Witness, this appears to be a document signed by Mr. Tuta, dated the 5th of October, 1993, and addressed to Mr. Stampar. And he says that he lends you 15 -- that Mr. Stampar is being given 15 men [redacted]

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Witness, I'll repeat the question: Do you recall that in fact were you actually taken --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Mr. Bos.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Witness, you've read the document. Do you recall that you were actually taken under the command of Mr. Stampar in that period?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NT
utterances.text: No. I do not, and this is the first time that I see this paper. My name is on it. Had it been true, I'd also have a paper with Mr. Stampar's order.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: So is it your testimony that you never worked under the command of Mr. Stampar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NT
utterances.text: No. I did not say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Which periods did you work under the command of Mr. Stampar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NT
utterances.text: Under Mr. Stampar's command, I never was under his command. I was under the operative command in Mostar, the operative zone command in Mostar, which means that I was a sabotage platoon or squad or company. We were a few. And we were always on the alert, whenever there was need to go to the front line, to replace, we did that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: But if there was a need to go to the front line, and the front line was in the area of responsibility of Mr. Stampar, would you then not fall under the command of Mr. Stampar? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NT
utterances.text: Mr. Stampar could ask the commander of the operative zone some reinforcements, but this paper, I would have seen before. I would have had the paper, and I would follow the order.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Witness, this document says that -- the last sentence of this message from Mr. Tuta says, "Orders can only be issued through the Convicts Battalion." What would that mean?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NT
utterances.text: I cannot answer that because I was never the Convicts Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: All right. Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Could the witness be shown Exhibit P734?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Witness, before we go to that next document, let me just ask you one more question, because you never answered my question whether you ever worked under the command of Mr. Stampar. I've put it to you twice but you never gave me a clear-cut response. Did you ever work under the command of Mr. Stampar? You could say yes or no.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS NT
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: All right. Let's move on to Exhibit P734. Maybe out of an abundance of caution we could go into private session, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we will go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Witness, yes, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I'm not sure it will be very civil on my side but perhaps we could finish the witness today. I have only five minutes to spend with this witness, unless of course you have very many questions. If you do not, perhaps we could finish this witness today. If you do, then he will have to come back tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I'm afraid we have to stop at 7.00 because some of the staff has been working here from 9.00 in the morning. We already have three minutes past. Witness, I'm sorry that I have to keep you here for another night. You have to understand you are still under the oath during your stay in The Hague so do not talk to anybody about your testimony and do not let anybody talk to you about it. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We will resume tomorrow afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: 7.03 p.m., to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 3rd day of June, 2002, at 2.15 p.m.
